headline: Gusty southwest winds of 30 to 40 mph continue Friday with light wintry weather near the Tennessee border, then a quick weekend warm-up leads to a fast-moving band of rain and wind Sunday into early Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Around Charlotte and the rest of the lower elevations, Friday stays windy with southwest gusts of 30 to 40 mph and occasional higher gusts, just below Wind Advisory levels but strong enough to blow around loose objects and cause localized power outages. Winds ease Friday evening, though some lighter gusts linger, and low clouds may be stubborn before gradually lifting and breaking up in the afternoon and evening. In the North Carolina mountains near the Tennessee border, snow with possible sleet and light freezing drizzle continues into Friday evening, with 1 to 3 inches (locally more) on the higher elevations of western Graham and Macon Counties this morning, slick high-elevation roads and negligible ice. Mountain winds pick up again Friday night, with gusts over 40 mph likely above 3,500 feet, especially in the northern North Carolina mountains, into early Saturday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is dry, and temperatures warm quickly through the weekend ahead of the next cold front. That fast-moving front brings rain to the whole region Sunday afternoon into Sunday night along with more gusty winds, with about 0.5 to 0.75 inch in the western half of the area and 0.1 to 0.4 inch in the east, including the Charlotte area; the flooding threat looks minimal. It will be warm enough for all rain, except for a brief chance of snow showers on the higher elevations along the North Carolina–Tennessee border late Sunday night into early Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Monday through Thursday look dry across the region. Temperatures should be near normal Monday and Tuesday, then warm to above normal by Wednesday.

watch_for: Gusts of 30 to 40 mph Friday, and over 40 mph in the high mountains Friday night, with possible localized power outages
Slick high-elevation roads and light freezing drizzle near the Tennessee border Friday
Sunday's fast-moving rain and gusty winds, with amounts trending a bit higher in the west
confidence: Forecasters made no major changes and are confident in Friday's gusty winds staying just below advisory levels, in rain for everyone late Sunday, and in dry weather Monday through Thursday.
